evidence_model.interpretation: The evidence_state field is a compact primary index for a bounded claim. It is not an exhaustive inventory of every evidence dimension satisfied by the target, and counts of this field must not be used to infer global absence of activation, durability, or verification.
machine_reader_rules: Resolve target and environment before interpreting an evidence label.
Do not infer system-wide absence from counts of the legacy evidence_state field.
Treat DOCUMENTED, IMPLEMENTED, TESTED, ACTIVATED, DURABLE, and INDEPENDENTLY_VERIFIED as distinct claim dimensions rather than mutually exclusive project phases.
Keep positive and negative evidence together; a failed invariant remains failed even when deployment reachability or other mechanism checks pass.
Do not globalize a bounded failure into nonexistence of the entire capability family unless the cited evidence supports that stronger claim.
Preserve claim ceilings: staging activation is not production replacement, bounded persistence is not universal durability, and operator-run evidence is not independent third-party certification.

current_production.basis: Deployed Python/state were inspected on 2026-08-14 and a retained 2026-08-18 black-box campaign traversed the existing deployment through the private validation-target integration.
current_production.durability_ceiling: Six persistence barriers and deterministic session mapping were observed in the August 18 campaign, but cross-conversation continuity and correction persistence failed the fixed-invariant suite; no blanket durability claim is made.

v5.basis: Pinned V5 CI is green and the accepted staging release completed deploy-test successfully; deploy-production was skipped.

evidence_states.DOCUMENTED: Design, responsibility, or claim is recorded without a stronger runtime evidence tier being implied.
evidence_states.IMPLEMENTED: Concrete source/schema/call-site evidence materially represents the responsibility; not necessarily exercised or deployed.
evidence_states.TESTED: Assertion-bearing tests, retained runs, benchmarks, CI, smoke, audit, or acceptance evidence exercise the bounded claim.
evidence_states.ACTIVATED: Evidence shows the identified path is operationally enabled/reachable in the identified environment.
evidence_states.DURABLE: Evidence shows relevant state/effects survive the required lifecycle, restart, or time boundary.
evidence_states.INDEPENDENTLY_VERIFIED: An applicable external or independent validation event supports the bounded claim.
evidence_states.ARCHIVED_SUPERSEDED: Path existed but is replaced, disabled, or no longer authoritative.
evidence_states.LINEAGE_INFERRED: Relationship is reconstructed across sources rather than explicitly stated contemporaneously.

claims.claim: Nexus Synapse is the private parent runtime; the public repositories are bounded reference/evidence surfaces rather than a public reconstruction kit.

Nexus subsystem names are project vocabulary rather than novelty evidence by themselves; the portfolio maps them to closest conventional systems concepts and separates that mapping from Nexus-specific composition/authority decisions.
Public Nexus claims are governed by change-triggered reconciliation, weekly drift scans, monthly pinned-head reconciliation, and a full reconciliation gate before major public releases/submissions.

The Nexus public provenance operation was formalized locally with Moon Source's Credits & Attribution Ops Protocol as reference/inspiration, without claiming Moon Source authorship of pre-existing Nexus architecture or code.
claims.claim_ceiling: Documentation/governance-practice lineage only; no endorsement, partnership, shared ownership, architectural derivation, reuse permission, or external validation is implied.

claims.claim: Process Architecture v0.7 is the canonical approved public process-documentation release in the engineering portfolio, with Request Watch, Master Process Map, Value Stream, linked process WIs, governing control families, explicit evidence-tier labels, and V5 staging-activation semantics.
claims.claim_ceiling: The process map is navigation/documentation evidence. Its production/V5 badges reference separately pinned evidence and do not by themselves establish activation or durability.

claims.claim: The V5 target process families shown in Process Architecture v0.7 are code-backed in the pinned V5 reconstruction snapshot and carry acceptance-test evidence from the cited green CI run.
claims.claim_ceiling: V5 code/test evidence only; it does not by itself establish staging activation, sustained durability, or production deployment. Staging activation is a separate claim with separate evidence.

claims.claim: The public process architecture identifies governing CTRL-* control families for material decision families.
claims.claim_ceiling: V5 is not yet claimed to bind control_id + approved_revision into every runtime PASS/FAIL decision receipt; that remains an explicit traceability requirement.

claims.claim: The existing Nexus runtime is operationally deployed/reachable in the production environment at the retained evidence boundary.
claims.claim_ceiling: Activation/reachability of the existing deployment only. This does not establish that every optional subsystem is active, every invariant passes, all state is durable across every lifecycle, or the full private runtime is independently certified.

claims.claim: The retained August 18, 2026 deployed-target campaign observed deterministic session mapping and six persistence barriers, with expected interactions and summaries present before the following turn.
claims.claim_ceiling: Bounded persistence evidence only. Cross-conversation continuity and correction persistence failed the fixed-invariant suite, so this must not be generalized into universal or sustained Nexus durability.

claims.claim: The accepted V5 release checkpoint was deployed to the controlled staging/test environment and passed the protected staging release path.
claims.claim_ceiling: V5 staging activation only. deploy-production was skipped; V5 has not replaced the existing production runtime and sustained durability is not established by one deployment event.

claims.claim: Nexus Proof Runtime v0.1.1 is a standalone receipt-backed execution/evidence reference kernel, not a production Nexus subsystem.
claims.claim_ceiling: Published security-hardening reference release; not a third-party security audit, production certification, or proof of the full production Nexus execution path.

claims.claim: Live Runtime Acceptance Rig v0.1.1 is a reusable live-boundary acceptance framework with durable readback and retained evidence, not a Nexus subsystem.
claims.claim_ceiling: Framework execution success does not itself certify a target or convert a failed target invariant into PASS.

claims.claim: Nexus Mode Card Creator 0.1.2 exposes behavioral-profile authoring while intentionally excluding private activation, weighting, persistence, and runtime integration.

Nexus Memory Kernel 0.1.0 is a standalone bounded reference implementation for scoped persistence, recall, correction/supersession, provenance, and memory-capability execution; it does not expose the private production memory/query or general-purpose execution layers.
claims.claim_ceiling: Public kernel behavior only; not current production Nexus memory behavior or private SSR memory selection/composition.

claims.claim: Nexus Black-Box Validation Gateway 0.2.0 is a standalone public challenge surface for opaque targets with BYO OpenAI-compatible inference handoff, public artifact submission, evaluator-authored challenge contracts, the nexus-blackbox-core-v1 suite, router-use verification, and sanitized evidence envelopes.
claims.claim_ceiling: Public gateway behavior and a failed August 18 deployed-target campaign only; not evidence that deployed Nexus passed the fixed invariants or any broader validation.

claims.claim: OpenAI-compatible Router 0.2.0 is reusable standalone infrastructure for short-lived BYO provider routing, model locking, streaming, tools pass-through, route lifecycle controls, SSRF protection, secret-safe failures, and secret-free usage readback without embedding Nexus-specific runtime logic.
claims.claim_ceiling: Standalone router behavior only; not evidence of private Nexus routing policy, runtime composition, or deployed integration.

claims.claim: ChrisAI Runtime 0.1.0 is a historically grounded executable reconstruction of the flat-file, pre-database, pre-SSR runtime lineage that preceded Nexus Synapse.
claims.claim_ceiling: Historical reconstruction only; not a byte-for-byte original checkout, not proof that every reconstructed line existed verbatim, and not evidence of modern or deployed Nexus internals.

claims.claim: A private Nexus validation-target integration has isolated CI evidence and was exercised against the existing deployment in a retained August 18, 2026 campaign.
claims.claim_ceiling: The fixed-invariant campaign failed. Integration reachability, passing persistence barriers, and a separate unseen challenge pass do not establish suite success, model-swap parity, or independent certification.

claims.claim: The retained August 18, 2026 deployed-target campaign observed deterministic session mapping and six persistence barriers, but cross-conversation continuity and correction persistence failed; a separate unseen challenge passed through all-session CAG behavior.
claims.claim_ceiling: FAILED fixed-invariant result. The separate unseen pass and mechanism-level subchecks must not be reported as a deployed Nexus validation pass.

claims.claim: Historical SSR work used structured SQL filtering/scoping before selective context injection and is an ancestor of broader later context reconstruction.
claims.claim_ceiling: Historical benchmark/lineage only; not current private SSR performance.

claims.claim: Public Technical Reference v1.1 separates August 14, 2026 deployed-code/read-only-state findings from older isolated execution receipts at a public-safe responsibility level.
claims.claim_ceiling: Dated production code/data inspection plus dated execution evidence; not a live August 26 trace, independent certification, or current V5 implementation status.

claims.claim: V5 is the target Nexus runtime reconstruction line: the production responsibility pattern is the parity source, while V5 introduces clearer contracts and approved hardening around those responsibilities.
